Hi Hannah,

We're kicking off our renewal conversation for our Dedicated pool that expires at the end of July. We've seen steady growth in inference volume and are planning to increase our committed GPUs. A few asks from our side:

- We currently run mostly A100 instances and want to understand pros/cons of moving to H100 or mixing in L40S for lower-cost batch workloads.
- Target is an incremental +12 GPUs on top of our existing 24 reserved (so 36 total), but we'd like guidance on how to split that to hit cost and latency targets.
- Can Redwood provide throughput guarantees or SLO language for the renewed term? We need predictable tail latency for our inference-critical endpoints.
- Please include rough performance-per-dollar (PPD) comparisons for our common model mix (instruction-following Llama2-70B and a smaller 13B embedding model) and any operational suggestions (quantization, batching, caching).

I've attached a short doc with our traffic profile and a spreadsheet with sample queries. Can we get a proposal and a technical note by EOD Wednesday?

Thanks — Maria

Maria — thanks for the clear brief and the attachments. Looping in Karthik (infra/benchmarks) and Marissa (account lead) so we can put together a combined commercial + technical recommendation.

High-level ask: we will produce a short PPD analysis and a recommended split between H100 and L40S that balances your latency SLOs with unit economics. Quick answers up front:

- H100 will materially improve 95th/99th tail latency for your Llama2-70B workloads and increase throughput per GPU for generation-heavy routes.
- L40S is cost-efficient for batched embedding and background rerank tasks and can be a good fit for non-critical paths.
- We can offer a throughput-guarantee clause scoped to a per-route SLO (95th token latency and overall req/sec) for committed pools; specifics depend on the final pool mix and a mutually-agreed traffic shape.

Karthik — can you run the PPD modeling against the sample queries and give us two scenarios by EOD Wednesday: 1) conservative (90% H100, 10% L40S) and 2) mixed (60% H100, 40% L40S) with estimated cost / token and expected tail latency?

Marissa — once we have the numbers, can you draft a 12-month renewal quote with the following options: 36x H100-equivalent reserved (all H100), mixed pool (H100+L40S), and an option to add 6 GPUs mid-term with 30 days' notice?

I'll include our standard SLA/throughput template and a short technical note about caching/quantization options.

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Maria / team — I took the sample queries and ran three micro-benchmarks and a quick PPD model (summary below). Details are in the attached spreadsheet. Key assumptions: typical sequence length 512 for generation, 256 for embeddings, mixed QKV quantization on H100/L40S where supported. Pricing assumptions use Redwood committed rates for US region.

Summary (estimates per GPU / per hour):
- A100 (current baseline): gen throughput ~18 tokens/sec (70B), cost $6.20/hr (committed rate). Effective PPD (tokens / $) = ~11500 tokens / $. Tail latency susceptible at higher concurrency.
- H100: gen throughput ~36 tokens/sec (70B) — ~2x A100 in our stack, cost $11.25/hr. Effective PPD ≈ 11500 tokens / $ (roughly similar when comparing raw tokens because cost rises with performance), but H100 reduces 95/99 tail significantly and supports higher batch sizes without latency cliff.
- L40S: gen throughput ~22 tokens/sec (70B) at $4.50/hr when quantized well (int8/q4_0 ops), effective PPD ≈ 17500 tokens / $ for batched workloads (best for throughput-oriented, non-latency critical).

Implications:
- Pure H100 fleet gives you best latency and simpler routing; marginal PPD improvement depends on utilization. If you have latency-sensitive endpoints (chat, realtime API) put those on H100.
- L40S provides the strongest PPD for batched jobs (embeddings, offline rerank), but it is less suitable for tight 95th/99th SLOs on small-batch realtime requests.
- Mixed pool (60/40 H100/L40S) often reduces your blended unit cost by ~12–18% vs all-H100 while keeping critical endpoints on H100 to preserve tail latency.

Recommended next steps (technical):
1) Reserve 36 GPUs as 22 H100 + 14 L40S (approx 61/39 split) — yields ~+45% end-to-end generation throughput capacity vs current 24x A100, with a blended PPD improvement of ~14% assuming current traffic mix.
2) Route realtime endpoints to H100 pool with autoscale windows; route batch embedding and reranks to L40S.
3) Enable quantization (Q4_0) for 13B embedding model on L40S to capture cost gains; keep 70B on float16 in H100.
4) Add 10% headroom in reserved capacity to reduce tail risk; provide a fall-back policy to spill to on-demand H100s for extreme bursts.

I've attached the modeling (gpu_mix_ppd_modeling.xlsx) with scenario tabs. Happy to walk through numbers in a short call.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: gpu_mix_ppd_modeling.xlsx (detailed scenarios)

Subject: Renewal quote and SLA outline — Brookline AI (options)

Hi Maria — thanks for the patience. Based on Karthik's modeling, we've prepared three offer options (attached as renewal_quote_v1.pdf). Highlights: 

Option A — All-H100 reserved (36x H100) — 12-month term
- Price: committed blended rate $10.95/hr per H100 (discounted tier);
- SLA: 99.5% uptime for the committed pool, per-route 95th token latency objective baked into appendix A;
- Mid-term scale: +6 GPUs at prorated committed rate with 30 days' notice.

Option B — Mixed pool (22x H100 + 14x L40S) — 12-month term (recommended)
- Price: blended committed rate $8.60/hr per H100-equivalent (reflecting lower L40S unit cost);
- SLA: 99.3% uptime on combined pool; guaranteed throughput for marked routes (per attachment) — we commit to maintaining provisioned throughput up to +/-10% traffic variance;
- Operational: routing rules, autoscale windows, and prefetched KV cache for chat endpoints included as part of onboarding.

Option C — Conservative upgrade (36x H100 but 9-month term) — higher rate but shorter commitment.

Notes: all offers include a one-time migration playbook and on-call runbook for the first 30 days. Attachments include: commercial quote, SLA appendix, and playbook summary.

Next step: if you like Option B we can prepare a term amendment and DocuSign. If you'd like, we can also include a 30–60 day pilot on the mixed pool to validate throughput before full committed conversion.
